subject: Zephyr committed capacity: preflight throughput model and safety cushion
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@zephyr.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@zephyr.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing ask for committed tier

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Zephyr’s leadership is leaning toward a 12-month committed plan but we need a concrete preflight so our procurement and SRE teams can sign off. High level ask: can you model throughput (tokens/sec) required to meet our SLOs and recommend a GPU safety cushion (headroom) and fallback model plan if traffic spikes?

Quick context:
- Expected steady-state concurrent sessions: ~2,000 (mostly short chats, avg prompt+n tokens ~220)
- Target p50 latency: <= 150ms for generation (end-to-end token latency)
- Desired commit: 120M tokens/month initially, with predictable burst capacity for marketing launches (~3–4x for short windows)

Can you send a short workbook or a short-run math model we can share with procurement? Happy to hop on a call.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, ZephyrAI

Attachment: none (will accept your workbook)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask for committed tier

Alex —

Thanks for the clear brief. I prepared a compact preflight workbook that walks through tokens/sec math, modeled SLO fit at different GPU slab choices, and a recommended safety cushion for both steady-state and burst windows. Key assumptions are visible on the first tab; I called out conservative defaults for average generation tokens and model footprint so the numbers are procurement-friendly.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Modeled per-session average token generation: 220 tokens (as you noted)
- Baseline target throughput required to sustain 2,000 concurrent sessions at p50 <=150ms: ~3,900 tokens/sec sustained (generation-only)
- Recommended committed slab: capacity equivalent to 6x A100-80GB GPU-equivalents (or 24 quantized 80GB virtual slabs), providing ~4.8k tokens/sec headroom vs baseline and allowing for KV caching benefits on short conversations
- Burst strategy: reserve a small burst pool (2 GPUs equivalent) + automatic fallback to a smaller, cheaper quantized variant with slightly higher latency for non-critical requests

I attached: zephyr_preflight_workbook.xlsx (workbook), slo-fit-summary.pdf (one-page summary), gpu-slab-mapping.csv (internal mapping of GPUs to tokens/sec under different quantization/memory configs).

Next steps:
1) I’ll loop in our provisioning/ops lead for a short runbook and SLA language for the committed offer.
2) If that looks okay to you, we can convert this into a proposal for procurement + include an option for a short-term burst add-on during your launch windows.

Would you like a 30-minute preflight call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: zephyr_preflight_workbook.xlsx (xlsx, 240KB); slo-fit-summary.pdf (pdf, 120KB); gpu-slab-mapping.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr committed capacity: preflight throughput model and safety cushion

Looping through Marcus’s workbook — two quick ops-focused notes for the proposal:

1) Safety cushion recommendation rationale:
- We should quote a 25–30% operational headroom above the modeled steady-state tokens/sec to cover noisy neighbors, kernel jitter, and short-term KV-cache churn. That maps to the 6-GPU equivalent Marcus recommended (6x provides ~25–30% buffer depending on model variant).

2) Burst sizing and failover policy:
- For marketing spikes (3–4x traffic for ~30–90 minutes), recommend a reserve burst pool of 2 GPUs (cold standby) and automatic throttling to the quantized variant after a latency breach threshold (p95 > 350ms).

Also attaching a one-line SLI we include in committed SLAs to keep procurement comfortable: "Committed slab maintains p50<=200ms and p95<=500ms for primary model; automated fallback to quantized variant preserves availability for non-critical requests."

Naomi
Director, Dedicated Accounts Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr committed capacity: preflight throughput model and safety cushion

Couple of model-level clarifications and numbers to include in the workbook before we send to procurement: 

- Quantized variant throughput: +1.8–2.2x tokens/sec vs full-precision per GPU (depending on attention kernel choice). Use a conservative 1.8x uplift for procurement math.
- KV cache hit assumptions: assume 35% effective reduction in generation tokens/sec for short-conversation flows; works well with your average prompt length.
- Latency mapping (per-token processing only, excludes network):
  * Full-precision model on A100-equivalent: ~0.00018s/token (=> ~5.6k tokens/sec/GPU)
  * Quantized variant: ~0.00010s/token (=> ~10k tokens/sec/GPU) but expect higher tail latencies under memory pressure

Recommendation: present two capacity options in the proposal:
A) "Conservative commit" — 6 GPU-equivalent committed slab + 2 GPU burst reserve (our recommended safe starting point)
B) "Lean commit + dynamic burst" — 4 GPU-equivalent committed slab + 4 GPU burst pool (cheaper monthly commitment, more reliance on burst)

I updated gpu-slab-mapping.csv with the token/sec numbers per variant; please reference that sheet in the summary PDF.

Karthik
Head of Model Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@zephyr.ai>

Marcus / Naomi / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. Procurement reviewed the one-page SLO summary and the two commitment options; they prefer option A (6-GPU-equivalent committed slab + 2-GPU burst). A few asks before legal/procurement proceed:

1) Can you add a short paragraph in the proposal that spells out intended failure modes and automatic fallback behavior (we want the engineering team to understand when the quantized fallback will be invoked).
2) Please include the HubSpot deal id (we'll reference internally): ZPH-2027-031
3) We’ll need DocuSign-ready contract language for the committed slab and an addendum for burst credits — can your sales ops attach that?

If you can update the workbook and send a final proposal by EOD tomorrow, we’ll route to legal. Also, yes to the 10am PT preflight call tomorrow — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the clarity — excited to move forward.

—Alex
